The fetched result is unchanged: after a successful fetch, `<--to>/<--fetch>/` holds exactly the regular files of remote `<--remote-dir>/<--fetch>/` at fetch time, at the same relative paths with the same bytes, and nothing else, symbolic links followed as `scp -r` follows them. What changes is the transfer: files unchanged since the previous fetch from the same remote directory are not sent again. With an injected `FETCH`, boxrun calls it exactly as before and keeps no mirror. Without `FETCH`, boxrun keeps a local mirror per remote directory at `<mirror root>/<base name of --remote-dir>/<--fetch>/`; the mirror root is `$BOXRUN_MIRROR_ROOT` when set (for tests), otherwise `$HOME/.cache/metis-serve/fetch-mirror`.    163	  | Method | Acts on | p | Maximum factor k | bound |
   164	  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   165	  | data-parallel over inputs | whole workload | 1 | min(8, factor) | k |

   172	- `Amdahl = 1 / ((1-p) + p/k)` with `p = min(1, sum(actionable stage.wall_s) / total_wall_s)`. Fractions are recomputed from timings, never trusted from supplied `wall_fraction`.
